name: MS File Converter
tagline: Convert Thermo .raw, timsTOF .d, mzML, mzXML, MGF and more in your browser, msconvert-style, without uploading anything.
description: An in-browser counterpart to ProteoWizard msconvert. It reads Thermo .raw, Bruker timsTOF .d, Agilent and Mobilion data and the open formats (mzML, mzXML, MGF, mzData, MS1/MS2, imzML, netCDF ANDI-MS), applies msconvert-style filters such as peak picking, MS-level, scan-time and threshold, and writes indexed mzML, mzXML, MGF, MS1/MS2 or CSV. Spectra, precursors, activation, retention times, filter strings and instrument metadata are carried over, and mzML inputs keep their original XML. Files never leave your computer: output goes to a folder you choose or to your downloads.

wasm.source: src/runtime/rust (wasm-pack build --target web --release); wraps OpenTFRaw 3.0.0 (Apache-2.0, vendored + patched in src/runtime/rust/vendor/opentfraw) for Thermo .raw. Worst-case extra download: ~420 KB (page + Thermo WASM); Bruker adds sql.js (~650 KB WASM), MOBILion .mbi adds h5wasm (~1 MB gzipped), each loaded only for that format.

inputs.name: files
inputs.label: Input files or vendor folders
inputs.help: Add one or more files (mzML, mzML.gz, mzXML, MGF, mzData, MS1/MS2, imzML + .ibd, .cdf, Thermo .raw) or a vendor folder (Bruker .d, Agilent .d). Each input becomes one output. Nothing is uploaded; files are read inside this browser tab.

inputs.name: outputFormat
inputs.label: Output format
inputs.help: Open formats can be written; vendor formats are listed for reference but cannot be written by any open software. mzML is the PSI standard read by MZmine, MS-DIAL, OpenMS, Skyline and search engines.

inputs.name: mzBits
inputs.label: m/z precision
inputs.help: 64-bit keeps m/z exactly as acquired (msconvert default for m/z). 32-bit halves the size but rounds m/z to about 7 significant digits (≈0.0001 at m/z 1000).

inputs.name: intensityBits
inputs.label: Intensity precision
inputs.help: 32-bit is plenty for intensities (msconvert default); choose 64-bit only if a downstream tool needs it.

inputs.name: zlib
inputs.label: zlib compression
inputs.help: Compress binary arrays with zlib (msconvert --zlib). Lossless; usually 2–4× smaller. Every common reader supports it.

inputs.name: gzip
inputs.label: gzip the whole file
inputs.help: Write file.mzML.gz (msconvert --gzip). Smaller, but some tools (MS-DIAL) cannot open gzipped mzML; leave off for MS-DIAL.

inputs.name: combineIonMobility
inputs.label: timsTOF: combine ion mobility
inputs.help: Bruker TDF only. Off (msconvert default): one spectrum per mobility scan, with its 1/K0, which MZmine's ion-mobility workflows expect; a full run gives millions of spectra. On (msconvert --combineIonMobilitySpectra): one spectrum per MS1 frame and per PASEF/DIA window, with a per-peak 1/K0 array; much smaller.

inputs.name: filterText
inputs.label: Filters (msconvert syntax)
inputs.help: One filter per line, applied top to bottom, e.g. "peakPicking true 1-", "msLevel 2-", "scanTime [300,900]", "threshold count 150 most-intense". Use the Add filter list below for every supported filter. Leave empty to convert everything unchanged.

inputs.name: mzNumpress
inputs.label: m/z numpress
inputs.help: MS-Numpress linear prediction (msconvert --numpressLinear): lossy, with a relative error of about 2e-9 on m/z; much smaller files. Readers must support MS-Numpress (OpenMS, pwiz, MZmine 3 do; check yours).

inputs.name: intensityNumpress
inputs.label: Intensity numpress
inputs.help: pic rounds intensities to integers (msconvert --numpressPic); slof keeps about 4 significant digits (--numpressSlof). Both are lossy.

inputs.name: indexed
inputs.label: Indexed mzML / mzXML
inputs.help: Append the offset index and SHA-1 checksum (msconvert default). Lets readers jump to a spectrum without scanning the file. Turn off only for tools that reject indexed files.

inputs.name: passthrough
inputs.label: Keep original mzML metadata
inputs.help: For mzML inputs, copy each spectrum's original XML (every cvParam and userParam) and the header blocks, re-encoding only the binary arrays. Filters that change a spectrum regenerate its metadata.

inputs.name: includeMs1
inputs.label: MGF: include MS1
inputs.help: MGF normally holds MSn spectra only (msconvert writes MS2+). Tick to also write MS1 scans as entries without PEPMASS.

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.label: Overwrite existing files
inputs.help: When saving to a chosen folder, replace files with the same name. Off by default so nothing is lost by accident.

outputs.name: files
outputs.label: Converted files
outputs.help: Saved to the chosen folder, or offered as downloads.

outputs.name: queue
outputs.label: Conversion queue
outputs.help: Every input with its detected format, spectrum count, output name, size and location.

outputs.name: preview
outputs.label: Spectrum preview
outputs.help: The first 200 spectra written: level, retention time, precursor, charge, peaks.

examples.label: Synthetic mzML → MGF
examples.description: Converts the bundled synthetic mzML (2 MS1 + 24 HCD MS2) to MGF.

examples.label: MS2 only, top-20 peaks → mzXML
examples.description: Applies msLevel and threshold filters and writes indexed mzXML.

alsoCite.text: Chambers MC, et al. A cross-platform toolkit for mass spectrometry and proteomics. Nat Biotechnol 30, 918–920 (2012). (ProteoWizard msconvert, whose options and output this tool follows)
OpenTFRaw: an open Rust reader for Thermo RAW files (Apache-2.0).
timsrust: a Rust reader for Bruker timsTOF data (MIT), from which the TDF/TSF reader is ported.
Teleman J, et al. Numerical compression schemes for proteomics mass spectrometry data. Mol Cell Proteomics 13, 1537–1542 (2014).

seo.title: MS File Converter: msconvert in your browser
seo.metaDescription: Free in-browser msconvert alternative: convert Thermo RAW, timsTOF .d, mzML, mzXML and MGF with peak picking and filters. Nothing is uploaded.

faq.a: No. Conversion runs in a Web Worker inside your browser tab; the site has no server that could receive them. Output is written to a folder you choose or downloaded.

faq.q: Can it write Thermo .raw or Bruker .d?
faq.a: No. Vendor formats are closed and no open software can write them; they are listed in the format menu for reference. Convert to mzML, which MZmine, MS-DIAL, OpenMS and Skyline read.

faq.q: How does it compare with msconvert?
faq.a: Spectra, precursors, charges, activation and collision energy, retention times, filter strings and instrument metadata match ProteoWizard's output on the ProteoWizard test files; vendor-specific peak picking is replaced by a local-maximum centroider.
